description: High-quality answer criteria for the Performance Review - 90 Day Evaluation Getting Started interview. Employee self-evaluation approximately 90 days after starting a new role, joining a new team, or assuming materially different responsibilities.

terms.label: Role Understanding & Early Responsibilities
terms.description: The responsibilities, priorities, and expectations the employee understands to be most important during the early period in the role.

terms.label: Onboarding, Training & Ramp-Up
terms.description: Onboarding, training, guidance, tools, access, and support received and how it affected the ability to perform.

terms.label: Early Progress & Contributions
terms.description: Early results, accomplishments, and contributions and the evidence that supports them.

terms.label: Execution, Ownership & Follow-Through
terms.description: Follow-through on commitments, prioritization, accountability, and reliable delivery during the early period.

terms.label: Work Quality & Learning Curve
terms.description: Accuracy, completeness, thoroughness, and professionalism of work relative to what is expected at this stage of ramp-up.

terms.label: Communication, Feedback & Working Relationships
terms.description: Clarity, responsiveness, coordination, and effectiveness of communication and feedback with the manager and others.

terms.label: Challenges, Constraints & Support Needs
terms.description: Challenges, constraints, resource needs, and support needs affecting early success.

terms.label: Growth, Adjustment & Next-Period Priorities
terms.description: Lessons learned about succeeding in the role and priorities, development areas, and success measures for the next period.

responseProfile.stance: Performance consistently falls materially short of expectations.
Performance has meaningful gaps and requires focused improvement.
Performance reliably fulfills the expectations of the role.
Performance significantly and consistently surpasses expectations.

primaryQuestions.question: During your first period in this role, what responsibilities, priorities, and expectations have you understood to be most important?
answerGuidance: Your current role/title or functional position
The responsibilities, ownership areas, or priorities you understand to be most important
The expectations or success standards you believe apply at this stage
Which responsibilities are core to the role versus part of onboarding or early ramp-up
Any areas where role scope, decision rights, ownership, or priorities remain unclear
Any changes in responsibilities or priorities since you started

highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review 90 Day Evaluation

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Identifies the expectations, success standards, or contribution level the employee believes apply to those responsibilities at this stage
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review 90 Day Evaluation

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Distinguishes responsibilities that are core to the role from temporary assignments, onboarding tasks, or early ramp-up priorities
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review 90 Day Evaluation

highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review 90 Day Evaluation

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Explains how unclear role scope, ownership, decision rights, or priorities have affected early performance or confidence
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review 90 Day Evaluation

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Notes any responsibilities or priorities that changed after the employee started in the role

primaryQuestions.question: What onboarding, training, guidance, or support have you received so far, and how has it affected your ability to perform in the role?

How any gaps affected your performance, confidence, learning speed, or work quality
Specific support that would help you ramp up more effectively next period

primaryQuestions.question: What progress, accomplishments, or contributions have you made so far, and what evidence best supports your view?

What specifically was achieved, improved, delivered, learned, stabilized, or solved
Why those contributions mattered to the team, customer, organization, or role
How your progress connects to responsibilities, priorities, or expectations
Evidence such as metrics, deadlines, customer outcomes, stakeholder feedback, or examples
Work completed independently versus with guidance, review, or team support
Any expected outcomes that are not complete yet, and why
